grades.quote: When an SRET instruction is executed, SIE is set to SPIE, then SPIE is set to 1.
grades.reason: Directly describes SRET's effects on sstatus state: privilege level restored from SPP, SPP cleared, SIE restored from SPIE, and SPIE set to 1.

grades.quote: kernelvec pops the saved registers from the stack and executes sret, which copies sepc to pc and resumes the interrupted kernel code.
grades.reason: RISC-V xv6 passage that states SRET copies sepc to pc to resume interrupted code and mentions the previous mode in sstatus. It covers only part of the restored state and is not a full spec description.
Table of contents only. It lists section titles and says nothing about SRET behavior.

grades.quote: When executing an _`x`_ `RET` instruction, if the new privilege mode is `y` , then `ELP` is set to the value of _`x`_ `PELP` if _`y`_ `LPE` (see Section 22.1.1) is 1; otherwise, it is set to `NO_LP_EXPECTED` ; _`x`_ `PELP` is set to `NO_LP_EXPECTED` .
grades.reason: Describes one part of SRET's state restoration when Zicfilp is implemented: ELP is restored from xPELP and xPELP is cleared. It does not cover the core privilege and interrupt-enable state.
